timeRange.note: NHM gives 69–66 Ma. PBDB occurrences of P. wyomingensis are almost all Maastrichtian (stage 72.2–66 Ma).

lengthM.note: Single museum estimate (NHM); the skeleton is poorly known beyond the skull.

massKg.note: Single museum estimate (NHM); mass estimates vary widely between methods.

discovery.note: Gilmore described the species as Troodon wyomingensis. The genus Pachycephalosaurus was named by Brown & Schlaikjer in 1943, and the species now belongs to it.

text.en: Pachycephalosaurus was a two-legged plant eater with a large bony dome on its head, surrounded by spikes and bumps. Some scientists think it used the dome in head-butting contests, others that it was for display. It lived in North America about 69 to 66 million years ago, alongside Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops. Dracorex and Stygimoloch, once named as separate dinosaurs, may be its younger growth stages.
Dracorex and Stygimoloch, once named as separate dinosaurs, may be younger growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus: its skull seems to have changed shape dramatically as it grew up.

alt.en: Cast skeleton of Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis at the North American Museum of Ancient Life.

uncertain.note: Only a single museum figure (NHM, 450 kg) was found; mass estimates vary widely between methods, so this figure may not be representative.
